program.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Make this look like a comic book photo
requirements.source_phrase: Make this look like a comic book photo

outcomes.description: Transform the image so it has a comic-book visual style while retaining its photographic subject matter.
outcomes.target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book styling?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comic-book visual styling is visibly present; fail if there is no visible comic-book styling; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the overall visual treatment of the supplied image as edited, without requiring a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image retain photographic subject matter and appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the subject matter remains recognizably photographic; fail if photographic subject matter or appearance is not retained; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the supplied image as edited for photographic subject matter and appearance alongside any stylistic changes.

nodes.question: Does the edited image fully look like a comic-book photo?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 and s2 both pass. Partial if at least one passes and the requirement is not complete, including when the other is failed or unknown. Absent if both fail. Unknown if neither passes and at least one is unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; unresolved required evidence remains unknown.

The nested support check independently assesses photographic appearance, and the fulfillment rules correctly distinguish complete, partial, absent, and unknown using only support evidence. fulfillment: The binding’s ellipsis and “fully look like” phrasing leave the requested combination and completion threshold underspecified. Make the node explicitly assess the two already-defined requirements—visible comic-book treatment and retained photographic appearance—and apply the existing complete/partial/absent/unknown logic without treating either alone as full fulfillment. The traces consistently find photographic appearance retained but comic-book styling absent, so the reference “no” is consistent with the rubric’s absent category; do not relabel that as partial merely because the source subject remains photographic. Keep the visual criterion grounded in the edited image and avoid making any single example (such as halftone dots) mandatory. Separately, one trace is unknown solely because of an API transport failure, not contrary visual evidence; preserve that as an execution/dependency failure and retry or leave unresolved rather than interpreting it as evidence. Repeated high-confidence traces support the styling finding, while the single failed call should not override them.
s2: The node currently checks only whether photographic appearance is retained, so its repeated high-confidence passes cannot distinguish fulfillment of “Make this look like a comic book photo” from an unchanged photograph. Keep the photographic-retention check as a support criterion, but make its binding explicitly evaluate that criterion alongside the already-defined comic-book treatment and feed both into the existing complete/partial/absent/unknown rubric: retaining the photo alone is not progress toward the requested style. In these images, the edited street scene remains photographic and shows no clear comic-book treatment, consistent with “no”; do not count retained subject matter as partial progress or require any single stylistic device. Treat the API transport failure as an execution failure, not visual evidence, and retry or leave that trace unresolved.
s1: Repair the binding’s truncated/elliptical wording so this support node evaluates the edited image against the actual request, not photographic retention alone: assess visible comic-book treatment and whether the scene still reads as a photo, then distinguish complete, partial, absent, and indeterminate evidence under the existing rubric. The supplied edit remains recognizably a realistic street photograph, with no clear comic-book rendering; the repeated high-confidence traces support absence of the requested styling, not partial progress from retaining the scene. Treat examples such as outlines or halftone as possible evidence, never mandatory techniques. Keep transport/API failures separate from visual judgments: retry them or leave them unresolved rather than counting them as evidence. Do not force the reference label or infer atomic ground truth from it.

Unknown if neither passes and at least one is unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; unresolved required evidence remains unknown.
nodes.binding: Target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.. Reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book styling?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comic-book visual styling is visibly present; fail if there is no visible comic-book styling; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the overall visual treatment of the supplied image as edited, without requiring a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image retain photographic subject matter and appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the subject matter remains recognizably photographic; fail if photographic subject matter or appearance is not retained; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the supplied image as edited for photographic subject matter and appearance alongside any stylistic changes.

nodes.question: Does the edited image fully look like a comic-book photo?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete only if s1 passes (visible comic-book styling is present) and s2 passes (photographic subject matter and appearance are retained). Partial only if s1 passes but s2 fails or is unknown, because styling has progressed but the requested combination is incomplete. Absent if s1 fails, regardless of s2, because retained photographic appearance alone is not progress toward the requested comic-book style. Unknown if s1 is unknown; do not infer a visual failure from an execution or dependency failure. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
